commentary_segments.text: A single-loop topology is preferred for low-power designs since it is less sensitive to circuit non-idealities such as low opamp gain, switch resistance and capacitor mismatch. A clock is used of 4 MHz and an OSR of 100 to reach a signal bandwidth of 20 kHz. The coefficients are such that the same output swing is obtained for all integrators, which is about 80% of the reference voltage (which is 0.6 V) at an input voltage of −3 dB. The minimum-gain requirement is only about 30 dB. This is easily achieved by a low-voltage opamp as discussed next.
